query: For automotive exhaust catalysts, what single intervention could improve catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Implementing a closed‐loop high‐throughput catalyst optimization platform that integrates automated solvothermal synthesis, accelerated ageing, activity screening, machine learning, and Bayesian optimisation will yield automotive exhaust catalysts with superior activity and durability and reduced platinum-group metal (PGM) consumption compared to conventionally synthesized catalysts.
generation.material_initial_state: Automotive exhaust catalysts synthesized by traditional methods with high PGM loadings.
generation.intervention: Adopt a closed‐loop high‐throughput optimisation approach to systematically explore multi-element catalyst formulations, aiming to lower the PGM loading while enhancing nano‐scale active site distribution and stability.
generation.conditions: Catalysts are synthesized under controlled solvothermal conditions and evaluated under simulated automotive exhaust environments with standard temperature, pollutant concentration, and accelerated ageing protocols.
generation.structural_mediator: Optimized nano-structural heterogeneity and synergistic interactions between non-noble and noble metal sites that enhance catalytic site efficiency and durability.
generation.mechanism: The integrated machine learning and Bayesian optimisation framework guides the synthesis towards compositions that foster enhanced active site distribution and improved thermal stability. This leads to catalysts that maintain high catalytic activity and durability even with reduced PGM content by leveraging synergistic effects between non-noble and noble metals.
generation.predicted_outcome: Catalysts identified via the closed‐loop optimisation are expected to show at least a 10–20% improvement in catalytic activity and enhanced durability compared to the traditional catalysts, while using lower amounts of PGMs.
generation.baseline: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts produced by standard synthesis methods that use traditionally high PGM loadings.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold for catalysts synthesized via automated solvothermal methods and evaluated under laboratory-scale conditions that simulate realistic automotive exhaust environments. Extrapolation to full-scale industrial production and long-term field performance may require additional validation.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement, optimal composition ranges, and scalability to industrial settings are uncertain and will need to be verified through systematic experimentation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of catalysts: one set using the closed‐loop high‐throughput optimisation process and one set of conventionally synthesized catalysts with standard PGM loadings. Subject both sets to identical simulated automotive exhaust conditions, including standard pollutant concentrations and accelerated thermal ageing protocols.
measurements: Catalytic activity (e.g., conversion rates of CO and NOx)
Durability (e.g., performance retention after accelerated ageing)
Nano-structure and active site distribution characterization (e.g., via electron microscopy or spectroscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the catalysts optimized via the closed-loop approach do not exhibit at least a 10–20% improvement in catalytic activity and durability compared to the baseline or if they require similar or higher PGM loadings to achieve comparable performance, then the hypothesis will be falsified.
